title: cookies sessions token and JWT lifecycle tradeoffs
concepts: A browser cookie is a transport mechanism for a value; a server-side session identifier must be unpredictable, protected, rotated, bounded in lifetime, and revocable.
Bearer tokens grant authority to whoever possesses them. A JWT is a representation with signed claims; decoding it is not validation and a signature does not encrypt its contents.

JWT validation must constrain algorithms and validate issuer, audience, lifetime, and keys. Token type matters: access tokens, refresh tokens, ID tokens, and session identifiers are not interchangeable.

Stateless token validation avoids a server lookup but makes immediate revocation and permission changes harder. Short lifetimes, refresh-token rotation, or sender constraints address different parts of this tradeoff.
Cookie security attributes reduce exposure but do not make XSS safe or eliminate CSRF. Session management and browser threat controls must be designed together.
